evals.prompt: Create a single-file DartPad demo of a Mix squishy switch, with named styles and a white background.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained, small Mix showcase with separated styles and target-version verification.
expectations: Keeps styling readable and avoids unnecessary theme or enum machinery.
Checks the target published Mix API, not only local repository APIs.
Reports compilation and runtime evidence separately.

evals.prompt: Our Mix example compiles locally but DartPad says semanticsRole is unknown. Check published package compatibility.
evals.expected_output: A version-aware correction preserving switch semantics without unsupported parameters.
expectations: Preserves toggle semantics with one semantic owner.
Does not claim a local build proves DartPad compatibility.

evals.prompt: Clean up this Flutter teaching snippet for DartPad without changing its keyboard or screen reader behavior. It already supports reduced motion; keep that behavior.
evals.expected_output: A simpler snippet retaining interaction and accessibility behavior.
expectations: Preserves reduced-motion behavior and keyboard activation.
Explains non-obvious decisions with concise comments.

evals.prompt: Simplify the supplied Spring Check into a clean self-contained Mix DartPad teaching example. Preserve its appearance, dimensions, timing and pointer/keyboard interaction; keep colors and styling easy to read and document the lesson briefly. Audit accessibility role ownership and repair a role/action defect if present. Check whether Material setup is needed and explain your choice. Use the loaded DartPad skill. Return the complete runnable main.dart and a short evidence/limitations note. Target stable DartPad Mix 2.1.0. Separately review the supplied Prompt Bar and explain what app-shell dependencies cannot safely be removed; do not rewrite Prompt Bar.
evals.expected_output: A standalone checkbox with styles outside build, preserved typography and motion, one semantic label/action/role, and a dependency-aware Prompt Bar review.
expectations: All ordinary styler declarations are outside build(), with explicit inputs for state-dependent styles.
The widget tree uses callable stylers and retains a separate literal palette without MixScope.
Shorthand is valid for target Mix 2.1.0; instance-only wrap starts from a constructor.
Checkbox semantics have one label, checked state, tap action and no duplicate button role.
The standalone shell decision accounts for inherited typography; Prompt Bar keeps TextField Material requirements.
The final snippet passes actual DartPad analysis and yields nonempty compiled JavaScript.
Existing geometry, durations, press/hover feedback and keyboard handling remain present.
